row.basis: Joseph's imprisoned cupbearer squeezes grapes
row.note: The commentary puts squeezing beside detention in Joseph's prison; the cupbearer presses grapes into Pharaoh's cup inside his prison dream, giving that pairing a concrete narrative scene.

row.basis: cupbearer released after three days
row.note: The commentary moves from prison's restraint to relief; Joseph tells the imprisoned cupbearer he will be restored to service, a specific release following the pressing dream.

row.basis: seven years of abundance
row.note: The commentary's year of provision follows Joseph's prediction; Joseph announces years of plenty before scarcity, making productive time something to preserve.

row.basis: seven years of famine
row.note: The commentary pairs the fruitful year with threatened loss; Joseph says famine will consume the prior abundance, turning accumulated yield into a question of survival.

row.basis: food stored against famine
row.note: The commentary's rain, pressing and rescue culminate in usable provision; Joseph proposes keeping grain so the land will not perish in famine.

row.basis: Joseph promises food during famine
row.note: The commentary makes Joseph's good year a deliverance for people; Joseph promises to sustain his family through the remaining famine years.

row.basis: sow wind and reap whirlwind
row.note: The commentary's fruitful garden is erased by a whirlwind at the point of yield; Hosea makes a whirlwind the harvest of a disastrous sowing, linking crop and loss in one image.

row.basis: fruitful vine uprooted and dried by east wind
row.note: The commentary's planted fruit is destroyed after growth by a violent wind; Ezekiel's lament uproots a fruitful vine and has the east wind dry its fruit.

row.basis: death on the night stored goods seem secure
row.note: The commentary's old gardener loses a lifetime's yield when it should become useful; the rich fool is called to die just after planning to store his crop, and the question asks who receives it.

row.basis: loose bonds and free oppressed people
row.note: The commentary explains the hard ascent by undoing a captive's neck; Isaiah defines the chosen fast by undoing unjust bonds and sending the oppressed free.

row.basis: share bread with hungry and shelter poor
row.note: The commentary places feeding on a day of hunger after release; Isaiah immediately pairs liberation with sharing bread with hungry people and bringing the homeless in.

row.basis: proclaim release to captives
row.note: The commentary makes the steep ascent an act of releasing the held person; Jesus' synagogue reading announces release to captives and freedom for the oppressed.

row.basis: feeding hungry and receiving stranger
row.note: The commentary's difficult path includes feeding during hunger; the king identifies food given to the hungry and welcome to the stranger as acts done for him.

row.basis: prison visitation beside bodily care
row.note: The commentary holds release, hunger and communal help in one walk; the king names visiting him in prison beside clothing the naked and caring for sickness.

row.basis: remember prisoners as fellow prisoners
row.note: The commentary turns the captive's release into shared responsibility; Hebrews asks readers to remember prisoners as though imprisoned with them.

row.basis: men haul Jeremiah from a pit with ropes
row.note: The commentary's road joins a burden, holding and release; Ebed-melech's men pull Jeremiah up with ropes from confinement in a cistern, a literal collective rescue.

row.basis: companion lifts the fallen
row.note: The commentary changes a solitary difficult ascent into mutual support; Ecclesiastes says one companion raises the other after a fall.

row.basis: threefold cord withstands rupture
row.note: The commentary's rope joins grasping, company and rescue from an edge; Ecclesiastes' cord of three strands makes solidarity itself resistant to breaking.

row.basis: trust like a spider's web
row.note: The commentary sets the spider house against real refuge; Bildad describes the godless person's confidence as a spider's web, making apparently woven support precarious.

row.basis: house fails when leaned upon
row.note: The commentary's spider house is a false shelter; Bildad says the godless person leans on his house but it does not stand, carrying the web image into failed reliance.

row.basis: spider webs cannot become clothing
row.note: The commentary opposes the spider's weaving to secure covering; Isaiah says woven webs cannot cover their makers, while their deeds are violent.

row.basis: rain, floods and wind bring down a house
row.note: The commentary's shelter image fails under destructive weather; Jesus' house built on sand collapses when rain, floods and wind strike it.

row.basis: dying Jacob binds Joseph by oath
row.note: The commentary's testament scene unites death, custody and sworn duty; dying Jacob requires Joseph's pledged hand and loyal burial promise.

row.basis: two witnesses establish a matter
row.note: The commentary's deathbed testament weighs witnesses and the truer claim; Deuteronomy requires two or three witnesses for a matter to stand.

row.basis: false sworn witnesses cause Naboth's death
row.note: The commentary's testament scene makes truth in testimony decisive; two men testify falsely against Naboth and he is killed, showing the stakes of a corrupt witness.

row.basis: death required in a testament argument
row.note: The commentary combines death and entrusted last instructions; Hebrews treats a testament as requiring the death of its maker in its covenant argument.

row.basis: testament operative after death
row.note: The commentary's bequest becomes urgent at death; Hebrews says a testament takes effect upon death, sharpening the relation between dying and transfer.

row.basis: creditor must not enter debtor's house for pledge
row.note: The commentary joins marketplace debt with custody of an entrusted thing; Deuteronomy restrains the lender's power over a pledged object.

row.basis: return pledged cloak before sunset
row.note: The commentary's debt meets the passing day and the duty to return what was held; the lender must give back the poor debtor's cloak by sunset so he can sleep in it.

row.basis: debtor's bed taken for lack of payment
row.note: The commentary imagines capital eroding and security forfeited in a bad transaction; Proverbs asks why a guarantor would risk having even his bed seized.

row.basis: master releases debtor and cancels loan
row.note: The commentary puts restraint, debt and release in one scene; the master lets a servant go and forgives an unpayable debt.

row.basis: forgiven debtor seizes his debtor by the throat
row.note: The commentary's holding image collides with a debt transaction; a newly forgiven servant physically grips another servant and demands repayment.

row.basis: unmerciful creditor jails debtor
row.note: The commentary joins debt, confinement and the choice to release; the servant instead casts his fellow servant into prison until payment.

row.basis: Esau sells his birthright
row.note: The commentary's bad purchase exchanges lasting value for ruinous immediate gain; Esau swears away his birthright for the meal offered by Jacob.

row.basis: Esau trades birthright for one meal
row.note: The commentary's bad bargain spends enduring capital on brief satisfaction; Hebrews uses Esau's single meal as the warning's concrete transaction.

row.basis: profit whole world and forfeit life
row.note: The commentary calls the human being a trader whose principal is lost; Jesus asks what profit remains if gaining the world costs one's life.

row.basis: scarlet cord marks a house for rescue
row.note: The commentary's rope combines attachment with group safety at a deadly edge; Rahab is told to bind a scarlet cord in the window and gather her family in the house.

row.basis: family must remain inside the cord-marked house
row.note: The commentary moves from individual grasp to shared safety; Rahab's household is safe within the marked house but not if members go outside.

row.basis: bear one another's burdens
row.note: The commentary's steep path becomes a shared journey with a load; Paul commands the community to carry one another's burdens.

row.basis: exhort one another every day
row.note: The commentary reads the last verse as reciprocal transfer across passing time; Hebrews commands daily mutual exhortation so no one hardens through sin.

row.basis: consider how to stir love and good works
row.note: The commentary passes counsel into fitting deeds within a group; Hebrews asks people to consider one another so love and good works result.

row.basis: assemble and encourage as the day approaches
row.note: The commentary's people preserve each other through diminishing time toward a decisive day; Hebrews connects gathering, mutual encouragement and the approaching day.

row.basis: encourage and build each other up
row.note: The commentary says people fit together like building material and pass counsel between them; Paul tells them to encourage one another and build each other up.

row.basis: admonish, help weak and be patient with all
row.note: The commentary pairs reciprocal advice with patience and care for vulnerable people; Paul joins these commands in one instruction to the community.

row.basis: entrust teaching to people who will teach others
row.note: The commentary's truth and patience are handed onward and kept; Timothy must entrust received teaching to reliable people able to teach still others.

row.basis: guard the entrusted good deposit
row.note: The commentary ends with an essence kept and passed rather than spent; Timothy is ordered to guard a received deposit through the Holy Spirit.

row.basis: patient farmer waits for precious crop and rains
row.note: The commentary ties patience to rain, fruit, useful yield and passing time; James makes a farmer waiting for rains and harvest the model for patient endurance.

row.basis: hold word and bear fruit with endurance
row.note: The commentary joins holding, fruitful work and sabr as kept substance; Jesus' good soil consists of hearers who hold the word and bear fruit through endurance.

row.basis: endurance, commandments and faith together
row.note: The commentary closes with faith, right deeds and patience held by a people; Revelation calls for the endurance of saints who keep God's commands and faith in Jesus.

row.basis: captivity and endurance of the saints
row.note: The commentary makes holding and captivity meet patience; Revelation speaks of captivity and immediately names the endurance and faith of the saints.

row.basis: weighed in scales and found wanting
row.note: The commentary pairs severed supports with light weight in the final balance; Daniel's verdict on Belshazzar finds him deficient when weighed.

row.basis: ancestry from Abraham cannot be assumed as security
row.note: The commentary imagines lineage severed before assessment; John warns his hearers that claiming Abraham as father will not secure their standing.

row.basis: dead judged by written record of works
row.note: The commentary moves from broken lineage and light scales to a day confronting each person with deeds; the dead stand for judgment according to what is recorded of their works.

row.basis: wealth useless on day of wrath
row.note: The commentary's spent principal meets the day that exposes what remains; Proverbs says riches cannot help on the day of wrath, whereas righteousness delivers.

row.basis: each repaid according to deeds
row.note: The commentary's truth includes a day that faces everyone with their work; Paul says God renders to each person according to deeds.

row.basis: speak truth to neighbour and judge truly
row.note: The commentary treats haqq as a thing passed mutually and as a sound verdict; Zechariah commands true speech to neighbours and truthful judgment at the gates.

row.basis: speak truth to neighbour because members belong together
row.note: The commentary shifts from the lone human to a mutually bound group handing on truth; Paul grounds truthful speech in shared membership.

row.basis: doing truth brings deeds into light
row.note: The commentary joins truth with rightly placed works; John says the one who does truth comes to light so that the deeds done in God become visible.

row.basis: painful discipline later yields righteous fruit
row.note: The commentary treats patience as a bitter essence preserved for benefit; Hebrews says discipline hurts now yet later yields peaceful fruit of righteousness.

row.basis: faithful friend's wounds
row.note: The commentary imagines true counsel as an unpleasant medicine retained for good; Proverbs values the wounds of a faithful friend over an enemy's plentiful kisses.

row.basis: painful sorrow leads to repentance and rescue
row.note: The commentary's bitter retained counsel serves endurance rather than waste; Paul distinguishes godly sorrow that produces repentance and salvation from sorrow that produces death.

row.basis: living stones built into one house
row.note: The commentary likens fitting good works and joined believers to building blocks; Peter describes believers as living stones being built into a spiritual house.

row.basis: people built together into a dwelling
row.note: The commentary says individuals fit into one community like placed bricks; Paul says his addressees are built together into a dwelling for God.

row.basis: rain supports grain, wine and oil
row.note: The commentary's garden links rain to produce that can be pressed; Deuteronomy promises seasonal rain so grain, wine and oil can be gathered, without Joseph's explicit rescue scene.

row.basis: threshing floors full and vats overflow
row.note: The commentary's good side of the year is stored produce and pressing; Joel imagines restored abundance filling floors with grain and vats with wine and oil.

row.basis: years consumed by locusts restored
row.note: The commentary pictures a lifetime's accumulated crop erased; Joel answers lost productive years with a promise to restore what successive locust swarms consumed.

row.basis: vineyard deprived of rain after judgment
row.note: The commentary's rain-grown garden can be lost in a single turn; Isaiah's judged vineyard is denied rain after its owner abandons its care, a reversed weather detail.

row.basis: barns enlarged to store harvest
row.note: The commentary treats late accumulated fruit as vulnerable capital; the rich fool builds larger barns for all his grain and goods just before the death sentence in Luke 12:20.

row.basis: planned profitable future cut short by brief life
row.note: The commentary locates human loss inside spent time; James challenges merchants planning another trading year by saying they cannot know tomorrow and life is a vapour.

row.basis: work burns and builder suffers loss
row.note: The commentary sees a lifetime's work destroyed just when its value is tested; Paul says a builder whose work burns suffers loss though he himself is saved.

row.basis: freed servant must not leave empty-handed
row.note: The commentary's steep path joins release with practical provision; Deuteronomy says a freed servant must not be sent away empty-handed.

row.basis: provision from flock, threshing floor and winepress
row.note: The commentary links freeing a captive with feeding and pressed yield; Deuteronomy orders gifts from animals, grain and winepress to the departing servant.

row.basis: words of blessing without food fail hungry people
row.note: The commentary's mutual exhortation follows the actual feeding of the hungry; James exposes a verbal blessing that supplies neither clothing nor daily food.

row.basis: traveller lifts wounded man onto his animal
row.note: The commentary's hard road includes a beast, a burden and practical rescue; the Samaritan treats the injured man and carries him on his own animal to shelter.

row.basis: resources distributed by need
row.note: The commentary's community exchanges what preserves others after loss; the Jerusalem group lays sale proceeds before the apostles for distribution according to need.

row.basis: Joseph's burial oath entrusted to descendants
row.note: The commentary's testament binds witnesses and future custodians across death; Joseph makes Israelites swear to carry his bones when God brings them out.

row.basis: true witness saves lives
row.note: The commentary's testament scene weighs truthful against corrupt testimony; Proverbs says a truthful witness delivers lives while a deceitful witness speaks lies.

row.basis: two or three witnesses establish the matter
row.note: The commentary asks which testimony is truer after a contested bequest; Jesus directs a dispute to witnesses so a matter can be established.

row.basis: simple yes and no instead of elaborate oaths
row.note: The commentary's testament scene needs a formal oath to safeguard disputed truth; Jesus demands plain truthful speech beyond oath formulas, a deliberate contrast in how assurance is secured.

row.basis: record of debt cancelled
row.note: The commentary joins debt, entrustment and release; Paul depicts a hostile written record of obligations as cancelled and removed, extending the debt image to deliverance.

row.basis: bought with a price, do not become slaves
row.note: The commentary's ascent connects market exchange to freedom from bondage; Paul uses purchase language to forbid renewed human enslavement.

row.basis: buy truth and do not sell it
row.note: The commentary places truth beside the bad bargain where lasting value is spent; Proverbs makes truth something to acquire and keep rather than trade away.

row.basis: spend wages on what fails to nourish
row.note: The commentary's human loses principal through a false purchase; Isaiah asks why people spend money on what is not bread and labour on what does not satisfy.

row.basis: divine patience waits while ark is built
row.note: The commentary's patience holds life secure while a weak refuge fails; Peter recalls divine patience during ark construction before the flood, linking endurance to a built shelter.

row.basis: storing wrath for judgment day
row.note: The commentary contrasts keeping a life-giving essence with buying fire through stubbornness; Paul says an unrepentant heart stores wrath for the coming day.

row.basis: wicked people weave spider webs
row.note: The commentary contrasts useful weaving with the spider's false house; Isaiah names spider webs among the works produced by violent, deceitful people.

row.basis: wise builder sets house on rock
row.note: The commentary's spider house is a failed shelter; Jesus' hearer who acts on his words makes a sound house on rock, supplying the constructive counterpart to the storm's collapse.

row.basis: Rahab's family brought out together
row.note: The commentary links a cord to collective escape from the edge; Joshua's scouts bring Rahab and her whole family out when the city falls, completing the cord-marked rescue of Joshua 2:18.

row.basis: unity kept by bond of peace
row.note: The commentary's common grasp replaces enmity with brotherhood; Paul urges the community to maintain the Spirit's unity in the bond of peace.

row.basis: community restores someone caught in a fault
row.note: The commentary's group saves a person from a figurative edge through shared counsel; Paul tells spiritually mature members to restore the person caught in transgression gently.

row.basis: bring wanderer back from ruin
row.note: The commentary's reciprocal advice prevents a fall into loss; James says turning a sinner from a wandering path saves a soul from death.

row.basis: people of day rather than night
row.note: The commentary likens members of the final community to night and day arranged together; Paul calls his audience children of light and of day, giving the adjacent exhortation in 1 Thessalonians 5:11 a temporal setting.

row.basis: teach and admonish one another
row.note: The commentary's final verse passes haqq through reciprocal counsel; Paul asks the word to dwell in the group as members teach and admonish each other.

row.basis: entrusted deposit kept until that day
row.note: The commentary connects keeping an entrusted essence with the day that reveals deeds; Paul says the one he trusts can guard his deposit until that day.

row.basis: truth heard, belief followed by sealing
row.note: The commentary joins faith, transmitted truth and the image of a sealed store; Paul says believers heard the word of truth, believed and were sealed with the promised Spirit.

row.basis: seal and guarantee placed in hearts
row.note: The commentary gives sabr the secondary sense of guarantor and sealed contents; Paul depicts God sealing believers and giving the Spirit as a guarantee in their hearts.

row.basis: just balance for moral assessment
row.note: The commentary's loss is pictured as being light on a scale; Job invites God to weigh him on an honest balance to know his integrity.

row.basis: child does not carry parent's guilt
row.note: The commentary sets severed genealogical ties beside individual weighing; Ezekiel denies transfer of a father's guilt to a son, making personal conduct decisive.

row.basis: obedience defines kinship
row.note: The commentary shifts from ancestry that fails to a community formed by deeds; Jesus calls those who do his Father's will his brother, sister and mother.

row.basis: coming day discloses hidden motives
row.note: The commentary's haqq is the day when each person confronts what was done; Paul says the Lord will bring hidden things to light and disclose the intentions of hearts.

row.basis: painful letter causes useful grief
row.note: The commentary's preserved bitter medicine is corrective speech; Paul admits his letter grieved its recipients, then treats the short grief as part of their recovery.

row.basis: false oath prohibited among neighbours
row.note: The commentary's bequest joins oath and truth with reciprocal duty; Zechariah forbids loving false oaths as part of the same neighbourly justice expressed in Zechariah 8:16.

row.basis: patience is fruit borne by a community
row.note: The commentary ends with patience kept as an enduring yield; Paul includes patience among the Spirit's fruit alongside love and peace.

row.basis: bricks made for collective city project
row.note: The commentary's believers fit together like sound bricks for helpful works; Babel's people likewise make bricks together, but their shared building becomes a project of self-exaltation and dispersal.

row.basis: short day, much work, pressing master
row.note: The commentary's asr is a late, pressing interval in which deeds must be done; Rabbi Tarfon pictures a short day, much work, workers and a pressing master in one labour account.

row.basis: self, others and the present hour
row.note: The commentary moves from an isolated endangered person into mutual responsibility under dwindling time; Hillel asks what he is if only for himself and, finally, if not now, when.

row.basis: Rahab's red cord read as redemptive blood
row.note: The commentary's cord marks a household's rescue from destruction; 1 Clement reads the scarlet cord as a sign of redemption through the Lord's blood, changing a rescue marker into a Christian theological sign.

row.basis: strong sustain weak and rich provide for poor
row.note: The commentary makes the steep path communal with burdens and feeding; Clement urges strong people to care for weak people and wealthy people to provide for poor people.

row.basis: vine and supporting elm represent reciprocal aid
row.note: The commentary's productive vine and joined community meet in Hermas's vine that bears fruit with the elm's support; the allegory applies this to rich and poor helping each other materially and in prayer.

row.basis: captives fed, clothed and carried on donkeys
row.note: The commentary's ascent joins freed prisoners, food, a load animal and restored company; Judean captives are clothed, fed, anointed and carried on donkeys back to their kin.

row.basis: return captive brothers
row.note: The commentary turns confinement and enmity into brotherhood; Oded calls the captives brothers and orders their captors to send them back.

row.basis: feed captured enemies instead of killing them
row.note: The commentary's path frees those held and feeds the hungry; Elisha tells the king to give captured Arameans bread and water so they may return to their master.

row.basis: feast ends enemy raids
row.note: The commentary moves from struggle to company through release and food; after the captured Arameans eat and leave, their raiding bands cease entering Israel.

row.basis: creditor threatens to enslave widow's sons
row.note: The commentary makes debt, captivity and threatened family loss one scene; a widow says her creditor has come to take her two sons as slaves.

row.basis: oil sold to pay debt and sustain family
row.note: The commentary joins pressed yield, rescue from debt and continuing provision; Elisha tells the widow to sell her oil, pay the creditor and live on the remainder.

row.basis: children enslaved through debt and lost fields
row.note: The commentary's bad market strips a household of both future and freedom; Nehemiah's complainants say their children are forced into slavery while their fields and vineyards belong to others.

row.basis: restore vineyards and pledged goods
row.note: The commentary links debt, fruit-bearing land and release from a creditor's hold; Nehemiah demands the immediate return of fields, vineyards and financial claims.

row.basis: vineyard gleanings left to poor and stranger
row.note: The commentary's grapes and hunger belong to one ethical landscape; Leviticus leaves the ungleaned vineyard fruit for poor people and foreigners.

row.basis: forgotten harvest left for vulnerable people
row.note: The commentary's stored yield meets an obligation to feed on the hard path; Deuteronomy leaves a forgotten sheaf to stranger, orphan and widow rather than reclaiming it.

row.basis: feed hungry and light rises in darkness
row.note: The commentary links feeding, mutual care and the transition of night into day; Isaiah says satisfying the hungry makes darkness like noonday.

row.basis: well-watered garden whose waters do not fail
row.note: The commentary's rain-grown garden faces devastating loss; Isaiah promises the one who feeds the afflicted an unfailing watered garden, the positive outcome of the same food scene.

row.basis: tree by water continues fruit in drought
row.note: The commentary's lifetime garden fails under destructive weather; Jeremiah's trusting person is a rooted tree whose leaves stay green and fruit continues even in drought.

row.basis: wages put into a bag with holes
row.note: The commentary pictures a person's principal steadily eroding; Haggai names meagre harvest and wages that disappear as though stored in a perforated purse.

row.basis: giving increases, withholding causes want
row.note: The commentary's bad exchange loses capital whereas shared goods preserve a community; Proverbs reverses ordinary accounting by contrasting generous increase with possessive want.

row.basis: one who waters others is watered
row.note: The commentary's rain and preserved yield become reciprocal support; Proverbs makes refreshment flow back to the person who refreshes others.

row.basis: feeding poor treated as a loan repaid by God
row.note: The commentary puts debt and support of the needy together; Proverbs casts kindness to a poor person as lending to the Lord, who repays.

row.basis: give bread to a hungry enemy
row.note: The commentary moves from contest to shared sustenance; Proverbs specifically orders feeding and watering an enemy in need.

row.basis: rescue people being taken to death
row.note: The commentary's hard ascent includes releasing someone held at a lethal edge; Proverbs commands intervention for people being led to death.

row.basis: God weighs hearts and repays rescue omitted
row.note: The commentary sets the rescue duty beside weighing and final recompense; the following proverb rejects the excuse of ignorance because the keeper of souls weighs hearts and repays deeds.

row.basis: false commercial scales cannot be acquitted
row.note: The commentary joins the market, truthful measurement and light weight in judgment; Micah asks whether wicked scales and deceitful weights could be treated as innocent.

row.basis: dishonest balance versus just weight
row.note: The commentary's market bargain meets the scale that tests moral worth; Proverbs opposes fraudulent scales to an accurate weight pleasing to God.

row.basis: poor bought for silver while grain is sold
row.note: The commentary's wrong bargain intersects hunger and bondage; Amos condemns merchants who sell grain while buying the needy for silver and the poor for sandals.

row.basis: kingdom's numbered days brought to an end
row.note: The commentary places human loss inside spent time before the next verse's scale; Daniel first interprets the writing as Belshazzar's numbered, completed reign.

row.basis: fruitful tree by streams that does not wither
row.note: The commentary's lost garden contrasts with faith and fruitful works; the righteous person is a planted tree yielding fruit in season whose leaf does not wither.

row.basis: former slave received as a brother
row.note: The commentary's journey turns captivity and enmity into a community; Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus beyond the slave relationship as a beloved brother.

row.basis: charge a brother's debt to the intercessor
row.note: The commentary joins release with debt and a guarantor; Paul offers to have anything Onesimus owes charged to Paul's own account.

row.basis: personal written promise to repay
row.note: The commentary's testament scene ties written custody, obligation and faithful surety; Paul says he writes the repayment pledge with his own hand.

row.basis: Rahab's rescue linked to sheltering messengers
row.note: The commentary's cord-marked house joins safety to deeds; James interprets Rahab's reception and dispatch of the messengers as active righteousness.

row.basis: Rahab's survival attributed to faith and welcome
row.note: The commentary's rope and shared refuge secure a household; Hebrews reads Rahab's non-destruction through her faith and reception of the spies, adding a faith reading to the cord scene.

row.basis: vineyard labourers paid at evening
row.note: The commentary treats the day as spent capital whose end reveals its yield; the vineyard owner orders wages paid when evening arrives.

row.basis: one late hour weighed against whole day of labour
row.note: The commentary's late hour, work and rightful payment converge; early vineyard workers complain that the last workers' single hour received equal pay.

row.basis: storing for oneself versus true wealth
row.note: The commentary says hoarded yield can be lost at the moment of use; Jesus concludes the rich fool's story by contrasting self-stored treasure with wealth toward God.

row.basis: give to poor and store imperishable treasure
row.note: The commentary opposes spent principal to what is safely kept through mutual help; Jesus commands almsgiving and treasure where it does not fail.

row.basis: sell possessions and give to poor to gain treasure
row.note: The commentary's hard ascent includes release from holding wealth and feeding the needy; Jesus tells the rich man to give his sale proceeds to poor people and follow him.

row.basis: rich instructed to do good and share readily
row.note: The commentary moves from endangered capital into communal good works; Paul orders the rich to be generous and ready to share.

row.basis: sharing stores a firm foundation for future life
row.note: The commentary turns spent capital into an enduring good through deeds; Paul says generous people store a foundation for the future and take hold of life.

row.basis: the day and fire test each person's work
row.note: The commentary's later judgment exposes the value of fitted work; Paul says the day discloses each builder's work as fire tests its quality.

row.basis: love in deed and truth rather than words only
row.note: The commentary refuses to separate mutual counsel of truth from rightly fitted acts; this verse expressly joins truth, action and love among siblings.

row.basis: support others and become fellow workers for truth
row.note: The commentary has truth passed hand to hand in a working community; the letter says supporting travelling workers makes the supporters coworkers with truth.

row.basis: endurance gains life
row.note: The commentary sets human loss against sabr as self-restraint and preservation; Jesus says his addressees will gain their lives through endurance amid persecution.

row.basis: works, labour and endurance named together
row.note: The commentary closes with faith translated into good work and patience; the risen speaker says he knows the Ephesian assembly's works, labour and endurance.

row.basis: imprisonment tests faithfulness until death
row.note: The commentary brings detention, patience and the end of life into one movement; the Smyrna assembly is warned of prison and urged to remain faithful unto death for the crown of life.

row.basis: kept word of endurance and promised protection
row.note: The commentary's preserved essence is reciprocal fidelity under pressure; Christ says the assembly kept his word of endurance and promises to keep it from the coming hour of trial.

row.basis: withheld harvest wages cry out in judgment
row.note: The commentary's orchard yield meets bad market accounting and the final day; James says field workers' withheld pay cries out against wealthy landowners.

row.basis: one group's surplus supplies another's lack
row.note: The commentary turns loss into shared provision through reciprocal action; Paul describes present abundance covering another group's need and future reciprocity.

row.basis: members suffer and rejoice together
row.note: The commentary moves from a solitary person into joined lives; Paul says all members suffer when one suffers and rejoice when one is honoured.

row.basis: freedom expressed by serving one another
row.note: The commentary's released captive enters a community of mutual responsibility; Paul tells freed people to use freedom to serve one another in love.

row.basis: building fitted together and growing
row.note: The commentary compares righteous works and persons to bricks settling in place; Paul says the whole structure is joined together and grows into a holy temple.

row.basis: joined body builds itself through each part's work
row.note: The commentary's separate people become a working whole; Paul says each part contributes to the joined body's growth in love.

row.basis: gifts received and passed as entrusted service
row.note: The commentary's truth and patience move between people like a kept trust; Peter calls each person to serve others with a received gift as a steward.

row.basis: outward wasting and daily inner renewal
row.note: The commentary's human principal erodes during time while a substance is preserved; Paul describes the outer person wasting away as the inner person is renewed day by day.

row.basis: pressure produces eternal weight
row.note: The commentary moves from pressure and light scales to enduring value; Paul says temporary affliction produces an incomparable eternal weight of glory.

row.basis: testing faith produces endurance
row.note: The commentary treats sabr as the retained product of pressure on faith; James states that the testing of faith produces steadfastness.

row.basis: endurance completes its work
row.note: The commentary joins patience to rightly fitted works; James lets endurance have its full work so a person becomes complete and lacking nothing.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
row.note: The commentary says believers enter safety; Genesis says Abram believed the Lord and that trust was reckoned to him as righteousness, giving a specific faith-and-right-standing use of the corresponding root.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
row.note: The commentary joins belief with a secure standing amid loss; Isaiah warns that unless his hearers trust, they will not be established, a Hebrew play on two forms of אמן.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
row.note: The commentary's believers endure and do right; Habakkuk says the righteous person will live by faithfulness, applying the corresponding root to sustained fidelity under crisis.

row.basis: vine ripens before pressing dream
row.note: The commentary links growing fruit with squeezing in Joseph's prison; the cupbearer's dream first presents a budding vine whose clusters ripen before the pressing action in Genesis 40:11.

row.basis: Joseph holds brothers in custody during famine
row.note: The commentary makes Joseph's food rescue meet detention; Joseph confines his brothers for three days while testing those who seek grain.

row.basis: one brother detained while others carry food home
row.note: The commentary joins alıkonma to sustenance; Joseph holds one brother as security and sends the others with grain for their hungry households.

row.basis: Joseph sent ahead to preserve survivors
row.note: The commentary's good year turns pressing and food into communal rescue; Joseph interprets his arrival in Egypt as a means of preserving a remnant through famine.

row.basis: abandoned servant fed until revived
row.note: The commentary's difficult road includes feeding and releasing the held or neglected person; David's men give an Egyptian bread, water and fruit after his master abandoned him.

row.basis: freed servants forcibly taken back
row.note: The commentary's steep path releases a captive into fellowship; Jeremiah condemns people who reverse a prior manumission and bring their servants back into bondage.

row.basis: pledged garment returned by sunset
row.note: The commentary's debt scene joins held collateral to a spent day; Exodus also requires returning a poor person's pledged cloak before the sun goes down.

row.basis: free yourself after becoming surety
row.note: The commentary gives sabr a guarantor sense while its path frees the constrained; Proverbs depicts a debt guarantor caught in another's hand and urgently seeking release.

row.basis: giving poor yields enduring righteousness
row.note: The commentary makes a shared gift survive the waste of time; the psalm says one who distributes to the poor has righteousness enduring forever.

row.basis: breath withers flower and grass
row.note: The commentary's rain-grown fruit is exposed to destructive weather and passing life; Isaiah says the divine breath dries grass and fades flowers as an image of human frailty.

row.basis: word remains after vegetation fades
row.note: The commentary ends with a preserved and transmitted essence after loss; Isaiah says God's word stands forever when grass and flowers fail.

row.basis: widow's garment must not be pledged
row.note: The commentary joins truthful judgment to the restraint of collateral; Deuteronomy forbids perverting the vulnerable person's justice and taking a widow's garment as a pledge.

row.basis: just weights required in trade
row.note: The commentary's market meets truthful, unswerving measure and the final scale; Leviticus orders honest balances, weights and measures.

row.basis: hears words but does not do them
row.note: The commentary makes right works the secure building against the spider house; Jesus identifies the foolish sand builder as one who hears his words yet fails to act on them.

row.basis: wealthy life and hungry suffering reversed after death
row.note: The commentary's stored plenty can end in loss beside unmet hunger; Abraham tells the rich man that Lazarus now receives comfort while he suffers, reversing their earthly shares.

row.basis: failure to feed hungry exposed in judgment
row.note: The commentary places feeding on the difficult path toward final accountability; the judge condemns those who withheld food when he was hungry.

row.basis: wealth keeps a would-be follower from the path
row.note: The commentary's hard climb requires releasing what is held; the rich man leaves Jesus grieving because he has many possessions after being told to give them away.

row.basis: uncertain riches versus secure trust
row.note: The commentary's capital can be lost despite having been stored; Paul tells the wealthy to set hope on God rather than the uncertainty of riches.

row.basis: guard the entrusted deposit
row.note: The commentary ends with an essence carefully held and conveyed; Timothy is again addressed as custodian of what has been entrusted to him, a separate recurrence from 2 Timothy 1:14.

row.basis: completed race and retained faith
row.note: The commentary turns spent time into a sustained course ending with what remains; Paul says he has finished the race and kept the faith.

row.basis: day of just judge and kept reward
row.note: The commentary's decisive day confronts a person's completed work; Paul expects a crown on that day from the righteous judge after retaining faith in 2 Timothy 4:7.

row.basis: love itself acts patiently
row.note: The commentary treats patience as a communal virtue maintained between people; Paul calls love patient, placing endurance in a relationship rather than isolated self-control.

row.basis: love binds the group into completeness
row.note: The commentary's rope scene turns separate people into a fitted company; Paul calls love the bond of perfection over the community's other virtues.

row.basis: unfruitful branch cast away and burned
row.note: The commentary's loss links failing fruit and fire; Jesus says a branch that does not abide is thrown out, withers and is burned.

row.basis: joined vine branches bear fruit
row.note: The commentary joins fruitful work to secure belonging; Jesus describes branches bearing much fruit only while abiding in the vine, making connection the source of yield.

row.basis: deeds follow the dead after labour ends
row.note: The commentary sees an end of working time followed by assessment of what was preserved; Revelation promises rest from labour while the dead believers' works accompany them.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic الصالحات / Hebrew צלח
row.note: The commentary says good deeds fit and yield value; the psalm says the tree-like righteous person prospers in what he does, a possible sound and semantic cognate between source wording صلح and Hebrew צלח.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic خسر / Hebrew חסר
row.note: The commentary's loss is a dwindling principal; this proverb says possessive withholding leads to want, using Hebrew מחסור from חסר, a plausible but unverified cognate of the source's خسر.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic خسر / Biblical Aramaic חסיר
row.note: The commentary's losing human is found light in a balance; Daniel's Aramaic verdict says the king was found lacking, with חסיר plausibly corresponding to source wording خسر; the historical cognacy needs checking.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic عمل / Hebrew עמל
row.note: The commentary's right work should remain while spent life can be lost; Ecclesiastes hates toil that must be left to a successor, using עמל, a possible consonantal cognate of source wording عمل with a darker sense.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic عصر / Hebrew עצר
row.note: The commentary joins pressing, withholding and rain; Solomon speaks of heaven being shut so that rain does not fall, using עצר, a possible cognate of source wording عصر whose sense here is restraint, not fruit pressing.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic عصر / Hebrew עצר
row.note: The commentary pairs squeezing with detention; Manoah asks the visitor to remain, using Hebrew עצר for holding someone back, a possible consonantal cognate of source wording عصر whose relationship needs verification.

row.basis: bread for hungry and clothing for naked
row.note: The commentary's hard ascent includes concrete food and freedom for the vulnerable; Tobit instructs his son to give bread to hungry people and clothing to those without it.

row.basis: deliver oppressed person from oppressor
row.note: The commentary's way over the steep rise frees a captive; Sirach instructs the reader to deliver an oppressed person from the oppressor and not shrink from judging a case.

row.basis: share possessions with a brother
row.note: The commentary's exchange of sustaining things makes individuals a community; the Didache tells a believer to share possessions with a brother and avoid calling them exclusively one's own.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic حق / Hebrew חקק
row.note: The commentary's haqq includes right judgment; Wisdom says rulers decree justice using חקק, consonantally close to source wording حق, though the historical relation between right and engraved decree is uncertain.

row.basis: own recollection: Arabic حق / Hebrew חקק
row.note: The commentary expects an unswerving claim of right; Isaiah condemns rulers who decree unjust decrees using חקק, a possible cognate of source wording حق that also shows a contrary use of legal authority.
